attempted_claim: Let A be a general Lagrangian with no decomposable vectors and let X_ord be a smooth ordinary and X_spe a smooth special complex Gushel-Mukai fourfold in the same fiber of the period map over A, with Hodge-isometric Mukai lattices and identified Hochschild homology HH_*. Bare same-fiber equivalence of Ku(X_ord) and Ku(X_spe) by Kuznetsov-Perry is assumed and not asked. Decide by proof or disproof the refined distinction question: whether the refined datum of Ku plus the rotation (degree-shift) functor, the distinguished Lambda_1 and Lambda_2 classes with their Bridgeland stability chambers, and the tautological Grassmannian action reconstructs the ordinary-versus-special type, i.e. whether every Fourier-Mukai equivalence Ku(X_ord) to Ku(X_spe) inducing the period Hodge isometry necessarily preserves the chamber and wall-crossing for the Lambda classes and induces a polarized isomorphism of the associated double EPW sextics and cubes, thereby distinguishing ordinary from special. A complete answer is either a proof that wall-crossing and polarized EPW data distinguish the types despite bare equivalence, or an exhibited Hodge-compatible equivalence identifying the chambers and EPW polarizations, proving refined indistinguishability.
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the refined ordinary-versus-special distinction was obtained. Only routine Mukai-dimension checks and a literature-gap analysis were completed; Bridgeland wall-crossing, rotation-functor intertwining, and polarized EPW comparison for same-fiber pairs remain open and would require tools beyond this one-hour pass.
